newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia lumber union says close to deal.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia lumber union says close to deal.

text.p: The union representing British Columbia coastal lumber workers said it believes a contract deal may be reached Thursday with the province's forestry companies.
Asked if an agreement could be reached Wednesday, IWA-Canada union president Dave Haggard said in an interview: "Not today. But I think by tomorrow we should have a deal."

He was speaking after the latest meeting with Forest Industrial Relations which bargains on behalf of 65 forestry companies. The chief negotiator for the companies also expressed optimism about the talks on Tuesday.
The two sides are likely to hold at least one and perhaps two further bargaining sessions on Wednesday, Haggard said.
They have been negotiating a new three-year contract to replace a deal that expired June 14.

Haggard said there were still differences on five or six issues, most notably wages. The union wants wage hikes of seven percent over the life of the contract and the companies are offering four percent.
Other outstanding issues are education funding, medical travel allowances, severance payments for plant closures and minor aspects of benefits, Haggard said.
The union represents 29,000 workers in the province's lumber sector. These negotiations cover coastal operations which also set the benchmark for contracts in the interior of the province.
